prompt:
A phone screen of the Monochrome music app's Social page, portrait, rendered edge to edge with crisp readable text, no device frame, no hand. The members of a small private instance see what everyone is listening to right now.

What leads: at the top a horizontally scrollable row of member avatars with small white thought bubbles above them (first "Your note" with a plus, then Mara "This outro is unreal.", Sol "Album of the year?"). Then the biggest gathering filling the width: a large album cover "Saltwater Hours - Cass Arlo" with two round avatars (Inez, Jon) seated on its bottom edge, "2 listening", a white "Join in" button and a "React" button. Below, smaller gatherings stacked: "Neon Margins - Juno Park" with Mara, "Slow Orbit - The Pale Hours" with Theo, each a medium cover with its seated avatar. The space is softly washed by the central cover's colours.

Monochrome's look: a near-black app ground with charcoal panels and faint hairline dividers, off-white text, white pill-shaped primary buttons and round icon buttons; the interface itself is colourless and every bit of colour comes from album artwork, whose hues softly tint the space around the largest covers. Titles in a tight bold neo-grotesk, UI text in a clean sans like Inter. Calm, spacious and premium, like a high-end music player, never a dashboard or a social-media feed. All album covers are invented abstract artwork and all names are fictional sample data.

Frame: a compact top bar with a menu button, the title Social and a messages icon with a badge "2"; a floating rounded mini player at the bottom playing "Weathervane - Cass Arlo".
